title: Five-core responsibility closure — authority/execution separation restated
summary: Governor directive 2026-09-29: restate the five peer cores as closed authority classes with explicit execution-power boundaries. permission-core = identity management + all directory/registry list management + codex governance-plane management (identity registry, directory boundaries, managed read-only registry paths, codex directory entry, codex read-session mint and dual-key grants; codex content authority remains the PostgreSQL codex itself). decision-core = all decisions and governance management with zero execution power (policy, priority, change, result acceptance; forbidden: directly executing module work). runtime-core = the sole execution authority (startup, process lifecycle, governed dispatch, execution validation; forbidden: self-authorization, policy modification). automation-core = all system-wide automation flows and orchestration without execution power (scheduling and dispatch decisions only; forbidden: generating permissions, accepting results). xingcheng-assistant = global review, inspection and audit authority (all typed receipts/audits converge into its review surface; forbidden: substituting user choice, persisting xingcheng data, acting as repair or upgrade authority). EXECUTION-BOUNDARY: business executes at the registered-module layer; independent tools are physical isolation containers (process tree, lifecycle, data domain, UI, owner root) and are not themselves the business executors; modules hold single owner, single primary responsibility and no independent authority.
origin: human-governor directive 2026-09-29: five-core responsibility and execution-boundary restatement (verbatim clauses: permission-core owns identity/directory/codex management; decision-core owns all decisions and governance with no execution right; runtime-core is the sole execution right; automation-core owns all system-wide automation orchestration without execution right; xingcheng-assistant owns global review/inspection/audit; business executes in modules, not in independent tools)

changes.proposed: SUCCESSOR:A604 continues to control five-core and historical-sub-sovereign responsibility convergence; this amendment restates RESPONSIBILITY-NORMALIZATION in closed authority-class form. CURRENT-PEER-CORES:decision-core|permission-core|runtime-core|automation-core|xingcheng-assistant. XINGCHENG native model remains a separate owned model identity and not a core or independent tool. SUB-SOVEREIGN-LAYER:abolished; former identities are retired lineage only. AUTHORITY-CLASS-CLOSURE:permission-core owns identity management, all directory and registry list management, and codex governance-plane management (identity registry, directory boundaries, managed read-only registry paths, the GOVERNANCE_CODEX directory entry, codex read-session mint and dual-key grants; codex content authority remains the PostgreSQL codex itself and amendment adjudication remains decision-tier). decision-core owns all decisions and governance management and holds zero execution power (policy, priority, change and result acceptance; FORBID:decision-core-direct-module-execution). runtime-core is the sole execution authority (startup, process lifecycle, governed dispatch and execution validation; FORBID:runtime-core-self-authorization|runtime-core-policy-modification). automation-core owns all system-wide automation flows and orchestration and holds no execution power (scheduling and dispatch assignment only; FORBID:automation-core-permission-generation|automation-core-result-acceptance). xingcheng-assistant owns global review, inspection and audit authority (all typed receipts and audit evidence converge into its review surface; FORBID:assistant-user-choice-substitution|assistant-xingcheng-data-persistence|assistant-repair-authority|assistant-upgrade-authority|assistant-learning-ownership). EXECUTION-BOUNDARY:business executes at the registered-module layer only; independent tools are physical isolation containers (process tree, lifecycle, data domain, UI, owner root) and are not the business executors; modules hold a single owner, a single primary responsibility and contracts versioned by internal timestamps, with no independent authority. FORBID:module-self-governance|module-cross-owner-execution|tool-as-executor-of-record. LANGUAGE-RESPONSIBILITY and CORE-LANGUAGE-ASSIGNMENT clauses of A604 remain as amended by subsequent landed provisions (B36/B162/B167/B38 Python retirement; native language pool C/C++23/C#14/F#10/Go1.27.1/Rust1.98.1/Julia).
